 Dated this the 10th day of July, 2025

Order 
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').
2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.702 of 2025 of Kannur Town Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. According to the prosecution, the accused had, from 2018 onwards till 13th January, 2024 entered into a sexual relationship with the defacto complainant under a false promise of marriage and thereafter subjected her to unnatural sexual offences and took the videograph of the instances of physical relationship and threatened to publish the same through social media and thereby committed the offences alleged.
4. Sri. Babu, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the entire prosecution allegations are false and the incident as alleged had not occurred.

It was also submitted that even if the entire allegations in the statement of the defacto complainant are admitted for the purpose of argument,
still it would only reflect a consensual BAIL APPL. NO. 7653 OF 2025 2025:KER:51405 relationship for a period of more than six years.
It was also submitted that the petitioner married a lady on 22.01.2024 and it was thereafter that the defacto complainant started raising allegations against the petitioner.

The learned counsel further pointed out that the statement of the defacto complainant does not reflect any promise of marriage and on the other hand, it only indicated a live-in relationship, which cannot be treated as rape under any circumstances whatsoever.

It was also submitted that initially, on 09.02.2024, the defacto complainant managed to register an FIR against the petitioner through her daughter alleging outraging her modesty and a learned single Judge of this Court had granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions.
Even at that point in time, petitioner had no allegation of rape and it is more than one and a half months thereafter that she has initiated the present FIR.
The learned counsel submitted that petitioner is willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed.
Rahul.

P.V vs State Of Kerala on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69863260/
2 5.
The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the allegations are serious and custodial interrogation is necessary.

It was also pointed out that petitioner is alleged to have sexually exploited the defacto complainant for more than six years under a false promise of marriage and therefore petitioner cannot be released BAIL APPL. NO. 7653 OF 2025 2025:KER:51405 on bail.

6. I have considered the rival contentions and have also perused the statement of the victim, which was handed over across the Bar by the learned Prosecutor as well as Annexure-V statement of the defacto complainant given in relation to another crime registered as FIR No. 104/2024 of Pariyaram Medical College Police Station.
7. The defacto complainant has, in her statement given in the present crime, has stated that after her divorce, the accused agreed to marry her, and that they had fallen in love.

It is also alleged that pursuant to a promise of marriage, they entered into a physical relationship and that the accused repeatedly raped her and even subjected her to various unnatural sexual offences apart from taking videographs of their physical relationship acts and subsequently he started evading from his promise of marriage.

8. Though the defacto complainant gave a statement as mentioned above, petitioner has produced Annexure-V, which is a statement given by her in a complaint filed by her daughter registered as FIR No.104 of 2024 of Pariyaram Medical College Police Station.
In the said statement, the defacto complainant herself states that for the last seven years, she had been maintaining a relationship with the accused, BAIL APPL. NO. 7653 OF 2025 2025:KER:51405
that too, even while her earlier marriage subsisted
. It is also mentioned that the defacto complainant's husband separated from her on account of her illicit relationship with the petitioner.
The said statement indicates that they were in a live-in relationship for a long period without marriage.
9. Long years of co-habitation without marriage, prima facie indicates a consensual relationship.
The petitioner is a 33 year old male, while the victim is a 49 year old lady.
They were in a relationship for the last more than six years.

The long period of cohabitation between the accused and the defacto complainant, without any objection from her, persuades this Court to prima facie assume that both of them were in a consensual relationship.

Merely because the defacto complainant has alleged in her statement that she was being raped, the same is not a reason for this Court to shrug aside the obvious, as revealed from her own statement given during the investigation into FIR 104 of 2024 of Pariyaram Medial College Police Station.
Ignoring such crucial material can tantamount to injustice especially when it may lead to depriving the liberty of the accused.

10. In the decision in Mahesh Damu Khare v. State of Maharashtra [2024 SCC OnLine SC 3471], it was observed that long BAIL APPL. NO. 7653 OF 2025 2025:KER:51405 duration of physical relationship without protest and insistence for marriage, would be indicative of a consensual relationship.

entities.text: Mahesh Damu Khare v. State of Maharashtra [2024 SCC OnLine SC 3471]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in Prashant v. State of NCT of Delhi [(2025) 5 SCC 764], the Supreme Court had observed that merely because a consensual relationship did not crystallize into a marriage, the same is not a reason to assume that there was a false promise of marriage.

entities.text: Prashant v. State of NCT of Delhi [(2025) 5 SCC 764]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

3 11.
The circumstances arising in the instant case prima facie, indicate a consensual relationship between the petitioner and the defacto complainant.

While considering the question regarding grant of anticipatory bail, it is relevant to refer to the decision Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1], wherein it was held that while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grant of anticipatory bail is a matter of discretion and the kind of conditions to be imposed or not to be imposed are all dependent on facts of each case, and subject to the discretion of the court.

12. In Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], it has been held that a mere BAIL APPL. NO. 7653 OF 2025 2025:KER:51405 assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the State has not been able to convince this Court that custodial interrogation is necessary.

13. Having regard to the above circumstances, I am of the view that petitioner can be released on anticipatory bail on the following conditions:-
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 21.07.2025 from 10.00 a.m. to 5.00 p.m. and if needed on 22.07.2025 from 10.00 a.m. to 5.00 p.m. which period shall be treated as limited custody for the purpose of completing the investigation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner, then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
BAIL APPL. NO. 7653 OF 2025 2025:KER:51405 (f) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
Rahul.
